title: The Coffee Cart
note: Tamsin brews something under the masts. She swears it's coffee. Nobody's brave enough to argue.

cast.name: Tamsin
cast.look: Side-on, older woman in a quilted apron and fingerless gloves, pushing a cart with a dented kettle on a coil of transmitter wire.
cast.voice: Wants someone to sit with her for one cup; warm, nosy, talks in run-ons and calls everyone love; measures everything in cups. Would never admit the beans are mostly roasted acorn.

open: Kettle's on, love. Sit. Nobody walks past my cart without a cup.
Real beans. Well, real something. That face hasn't slept since May.
walk_on: Suit yourself. It'll be cold when you come back, and so will I.
right: There you go. Sip it slow and tell me everything about the road.
Second cup's always better. Don't ask me why, it's the same pot.
You've got colour back in your cheeks. Another, then?
miss: Careful! I said it's hot. I always say it's hot.
Oh, it's gone down your front. Here, I've got a rag. Mostly clean.
win: Go on, then. Tell them up the road Tamsin's cart is still going.
bust: Right. Pot's empty, and so's my patience. Mind how you go.
spark: My sensors can't identify that drink. I'd say it counts as warm.

title: Up the Mast
note: Rook climbs masts for salvage. Getting down is a different skill, and Rook is still learning it.

cast.name: Rook
cast.look: Side-on, a lanky climber dangling on a snagged rope halfway up a radio mast: harness, tool belt, one boot missing.
cast.voice: Wants to get down without admitting they froze; sunny, loud, nearly every line an exclamation; keeps reporting the view to change the subject.

open: Hey! Down there! Lovely day for it! For climbing! Which I'm doing!
Small thing. Rope's snagged. Hold the bottom while I come down?
walk_on: No, that's fine! I'll live up here! Great view! Bye!
right: One rung down! Slow and steady. That's how professionals do it.
Getting there! I can see three dust storms and a goat from here.
Nearly down! Don't tell anyone I was stuck. I was resting.
miss: Heads! Sorry! That was my spanner. And possibly my lunch.
Rope jerked! Still here! Still very much up here!
win: Ground! Hello, ground! Here, I grabbed this off the top. Yours!
bust: You know what? I'll wait for the wind to change. Off you go!
spark: That rope has more knots than threads. I counted. Twice.

title: The Permit Booth
note: Pell runs the only permit booth on the tower road. Nobody knows who gave Pell the stamp.

cast.name: Registrar Pell
cast.look: Side-on, a thin official in a uniform jacket two sizes too big, behind a fold-out desk with a rubber stamp and a tower of forms.
cast.voice: Wants one traveller who fills in the form properly; florid, long words, quotes regulations; says every stamp out loud, and loves the red one. Would never admit nobody appointed them.

open: Halt. This road falls under the jurisdiction of the Mast Authority.
Passage requires a completed application. I am the Mast Authority.
walk_on: Unprocessed! Highly irregular! I'm noting this in the ledger.
right: Section one, satisfactory. Stamp. I do love a stamp.
Section two, in order. You'd be astonished how few manage it.
Countersigned. Stamp. Stamp. The second one was for pleasure.
miss: Rejected. That's the red stamp. I so rarely get to use it.
Inadmissible. No proof of service. Corporal, a scornful laugh, please.
win: Approved! And a spare form, pre-stamped. For emergencies.
bust: Application rejected. Corporal, file this one under Detained.
spark: I've scanned every frequency. No Mast Authority. Only Pell.

title: Hush's Water
note: Hush sells clean water and says almost nothing. The crew in the junk says even less.

cast.name: Hush
cast.look: Side-on, a hooded trader beside a handcart of dented jerrycans, scarf over the face, a tin whistle on a cord round the neck.
cast.voice: Wants your scrap and as few words as possible; one to four words a line; turns you down with a flat No; whistles to a crew hidden in the junk, once to sit, twice to come.

spark: Count the shadows behind that junk. Now keep talking nicely.

title: The Live Wires
note: Wynn guards a cache behind live wires and claims to know which are safe. Ask anyone with singed eyebrows.

cast.name: Wynn
cast.look: Side-on, an old lineman in rubber boots and a scorched coat, wire cutters in one hand, beside a hut wrapped in sparking cable.
cast.voice: Wants someone fit to take over the tower; gruff, dry, short sentences in wire talk; snips a wire and calls it live or dead. Would never admit they've forgotten which is which.

open: Stop there. Every wire round this hut's live. Mostly.
Want the cache? Earn it. I'll cut them one at a time.
right: Snip. Dead. I'm getting good at this.
Snip. Smells dead. Smell's a big part of it.
miss: Ah. That one wasn't dead. You'll get the feeling back.
Live! Sorry. I'd have sworn it was the green one.
win: Last one. Dead, I'm nearly sure. Go on in, the cache is yours.
bust: Not that one. No, not that one either. Duck!
Well. That was the main line.
spark: My sensors are tingling. Sensors aren't meant to tingle.

title: The Numbers Station
note: A voice by the masts reads out numbers with exactly two factors. It always stops at ninety-seven.

cast.name: Two-Three-Five
cast.look: Side-on, a figure in a padded headset at a folding table, cranking a hand generator, a long antenna taped to the chair back.
cast.voice: Wants to finish the night's count without losing the place; flat broadcast monotone, numbers in words; reads the primes in order and never says the word.

open: Twenty-nine, and then... Static took it. Help me find my place?
right: Thirty-one. There it is. Thirty-seven. Forty-one. Thank you.
Forty-three. Forty-seven. Fifty-three. The count holds.
Fifty-nine. Sixty-one. Sixty-seven. The hundred is close now.
miss: Forty-five. No. Nine fives. Forty-five is a myth, listeners.
Fifty-one. No. Three seventeens. Disregard. Sorry for the squeal.
win: On, and on, to ninety-seven. Nothing more before the hundred.
Two-Three-Five, signing off. Take the spare valves, listener.
bust: Too much static. Back to two, then. Two-Three-Five, going dark.
spark: There's a pattern in this. Give me a minute. Or a week.
